sugestoes.texto: The migrated host value is interpolated directly into SQL with `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` without escaping. Any host containing a single quote breaks the INSERT and aborts the migration; use `quote`/parameterization or `EmbeddableHost.create` instead of raw string interpolation.

`before_validation` calls `self.host.sub!(...)` unconditionally; when `host` is nil (e.g. the `host` param is missing) this raises NoMethodError during validation instead of producing a clean validation failure. Guard with `self.host` / use a safe setter so a blank host fails validation rather than crashing the request.

`update` and `destroy` use `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then call `save_host(host)` / `host.destroy` without a nil check. A request with a non-existent id yields a NoMethodError (500) instead of a clean 404/error response.

In the plural branch, `obj[k].map(...)` is called directly on the raw value; if the serializer emits a null collection (e.g. `color_ids: null`) this throws TypeError. The `hydrated || []` fallback only guards the map result, so use `(obj[k] || []).map(...)` to make hydration null-safe.

`execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories INNER JOIN site_settings ON site_settings.value = categories.name WHERE site_settings.name = 'embed_category'")[0]` raises NoMethodError on `nil` when no `embed_category` site setting row exists (the setting was optional and absent by default), aborting the migration before the table data is backfilled. Guard the result: capture the rows first and only read `rows[0]['id']` when `rows && rows.cmd_tuples > 0`, otherwise fall back to `uncategorized_category_id`.

The migrated host value is string-interpolated into raw SQL (`VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`) without escaping, so any newline-delimited entry in the `embeddable_hosts` site setting containing a quote breaks out of the literal and executes arbitrary SQL during `rake db:migrate`. Use a parameterized insert (e.g. `exec_insert`/`connection.quote`) for each `h` instead of building the statement with interpolation.

`before_validation` calls `self.host.sub!(...)` on a value that is nil whenever the `host` parameter is missing or blank (`params[:embeddable_host][:host]` is nil), raising NoMethodError instead of returning a validation error. Apply `host.to_s.sub!` (or guard with `if host`) so a missing host fails validation via `validates_format_of` rather than crashing the request with a 500.

`update` and `destroy` do `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and immediately call `save_host(host)` / `host.destroy` without a nil check, so a DELETE/PUT for a non-existent (or already deleted) id raises NoMethodError on nil and returns a 500 instead of a 404. Use `EmbeddableHost.find_by(id: params[:id])` and `raise Discourse::NotFound` when it is blank before proceeding.

The plural branch calls `obj[k].map(...)` directly on the raw value, so a serializer that emits `color_ids: null` (e.g. no associated records) throws `TypeError: obj[k].map is not a function` and breaks hydration of the whole payload, because the `|| []` guard only applies after `.map` has already been invoked. Guard the source collection first (`const ids = obj[k] || [];`) before mapping.

issues.descricao: EmbeddableHost's before_validation calls self.host.sub! unconditionally, so saving a record with a nil host raises NoMethodError instead of returning a validation error.
issues.textoGolden: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

comentarios.texto: The before_validation callback calls `sub!` on host without guarding nil. Creating a host with a missing or null host field reaches this callback from save_host and raises NoMethodError instead of returning a validation error. Guard nil during normalization and let presence/format validation reject it.

WHAT: `before_validation` calls `self.host.sub!(...)` unconditionally, so a record with a nil host raises NoMethodError (`nil.sub!`) instead of producing a normal format-invalid result. WHY: `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` directly; any request that omits the host value makes the save raise a 500 instead of returning the `render_json_error(host)` validation response. HOW: guard the mutation, e.g. `return if host.blank?` at the top of the before_validation block (or use `self.host = self.host.to_s` before stripping).

before_validation calls self.host.sub!(...) on a possibly-nil host before validates_format_of runs. The controller assigns host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host], so a request without a host key leaves it nil and nil.sub! raises NoMethodError at save time instead of the format validation producing a normal error response. Add a presence guard so validation reports the failure.

issues.descricao: update and destroy in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController fetch the host with where(id:).first and never check for nil, so an unknown id raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of not-found.
issues.textoGolden: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.

comentarios.texto: In the destroy action, the nil-host case (line 15-16) would raise NoMethodError. Consider adding a nil check to handle the case where the host is not found.

update and destroy fetch the record with EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first but never check for nil, then immediately use it (save_host(host) does host.host = ... / host.save; destroy does host.destroy). A stale or already-deleted id, or an interleaving where a concurrent delete removes the row first, makes host nil and the first call on it raises NoMethodError -> unhandled 500. Guard with a nil/404 check before use.

Update passes the nullable result of where(...).first directly to save_host, which immediately assigns host.host. Updating a nonexistent or concurrently deleted record returns an internal error instead of a not-found response; destroy has the same lookup failure. Use find or explicitly raise a not-found error before dereferencing the lookup result.

issues.descricao: record_for_host compares lower(host) against the un-lowercased URI host, so mixed-case referer hosts fail to match allowed hosts and embedding is rejected.
issues.textoGolden: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

comentarios.texto: Normalize the parsed hostname before comparing it with lower(host). URI parsing preserves hostname case, so an allowed entry such as example.com does not match https://EXAMPLE.com/page even though DNS hostnames are case-insensitive. This makes valid embedding requests fail the host authorization check and makes category lookup inconsistent for equivalent domain identities. Compare against host.downcase (or normalize both operands equivalently), and add a mixed-case URL test.

The query compares lower(host) to the un-downcased uri.host. A referer such as http://EvilTrout.com never matches the stored lowercase host, so embedding is wrongly denied. Fix: use where("lower(host) = ?", host.downcase).

The query compares lower(host) in the database with uri.host, which is not lowercased, so the comparison normalizes only one side. A referer or URL with uppercase letters (e.g. http://EvilTrout.com) will not match the stored host. Compare against host.downcase, i.e. where('lower(host) = ?', host.downcase).

issues.descricao: The migration copies the legacy embeddable_hosts values into the new table without stripping scheme and path, so hosts stored as http://example.com no longer match the bare-host lookup and previously allowed embeds are rejected after upgrade.
issues.textoGolden: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: migration inserts raw embeddable_hosts lines (e.g. http://example.com/123) without stripping scheme/path like the model does. WHY: migrated rows never match EmbeddableHost.record_for_host which compares bare uri.host, silently breaking previously allowed embeds.

Migration INSERTs raw embeddable_hosts lines with scheme/path intact, but EmbeddableHost normalizes to bare domain (before_validation strips protocol/path, record_for_host looks up by URI.host). Strip protocol and path before INSERT or migrated hosts will never satisfy host_allowed?.

Legacy hosts are inserted verbatim instead of applying the new model's scheme/path normalization. Existing values such as http://discourse.org or https://example.com/1234 remain in the table, while record_for_host compares only URI.host, so previously configured embedding hosts stop working after upgrade. Normalize migrated entries to the same representation used by the model before inserting them.

issues.descricao: The contents of category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb are swapped, so each file defines the other's fabricators.
issues.textoGolden: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

comentarios.texto: File named category_fabricator.rb now defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host) while Fabricator(:category) was moved to embeddable_host_fabricator.rb. Filenames disagree with contents — swap contents back so each file defines the fabricator its name states.

The file names and contents are swapped. embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines the category fabricators (:category, :diff_category, :happy_category, :private_category), and category_fabricator.rb defines :embeddable_host. Restore category_fabricator.rb to the original category fabricators and put the :embeddable_host fabricator in embeddable_host_fabricator.rb.

issues.descricao: The migration builds its INSERT by interpolating each legacy host value into the SQL string instead of quoting or binding it, so a value with a quote breaks the statement.
issues.textoGolden: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

comentarios.texto: The migration's INSERT statement uses string interpolation: VALUES ('#{h}', ...). This is a SQL-injection concern and should be fixed by using parameterized queries or proper escaping.
WHAT: migration interpolates raw host string into SQL: VALUES ('#{h}', ...). WHY: a host value containing a single quote breaks the statement and allows SQL injection via site_settings value.

issues.descricao: The migration reads execute(...)[0]['id'] for embed_category without checking for an empty result, so installs without that setting stored crash the migration instead of falling back to the uncategorized category.
issues.textoGolden: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: migration does execute(...)[0]['id'] with no guard when embed_category setting/category is missing. WHY: nil[0] dereference crashes the migration and blocks deploy on instances without that setting.
Migration does execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking empty result; missing site_settings row throws NoMethodError and fails migration. Check for nil row.

The migration indexes the first category-query result before checking whether any row was returned. An installation without a persisted embed_category setting, or with no matching category name, aborts migration before reaching the uncategorized fallback. Check whether the result contains a row before accessing its id and handle missing fallback settings as well.

issues.descricao: The spec 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' no longer sets up any host condition and passes only because embed_truncate defaults to false, so its name no longer matches what it tests.

comentarios.texto: Test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' does not establish the true-branch preconditions (embed_truncate true, has_topic_embed true) nor control host presence, so it passes regardless of host logic and would still pass if host checking were broken/removed. Set truncate true + stub embed true with no hosts for the false case.

The test named "is false if embeddable_host is blank" now uses an ordinary built topic without setting embed_truncate or making has_topic_embed? true. It therefore returns false for reasons unrelated to the missing host, and passes even with the new implementation that never checks host availability. If blank-host behavior remains the intended contract, arrange all the other prerequisites before asserting false; if the contract intentionally changed, replace this case with a test of the actual intended behavior rather than retaining a misleading passing test.

The description "is false if embeddable_host is blank" no longer matches the code. This PR changed Topic#expandable_first_post? (app/models/topic.rb:869) to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`, removing the embeddable_hosts condition entirely, and removed the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` setup from this test. The assertion now passes only because `has_topic_embed?` is unstubbed (false) and embed_truncate is unset, so the name states a cause the method no longer has — rename it (e.g. "is false when there is no topic embed") or set up the precondition it claims to test.

issues.descricao: The 'find embedded' test requests fruit 2 but the pretender always returns fruit 1, so it asserts fruit 1's colors and would not notice a find that ignores the id.

comentarios.texto: Test requests fruit id 2 but pretender returns fruits[0] unconditionally, so assertions on colors [1,2] never cover fruit 2's color_ids [3]. Make pretender honor :id or request id 1 / assert single-element case to actually verify plural _ids hydration.

This test now requests fruit 2 but expects fruit 1's two colors. The /fruits/:id Pretender handler always returns fruits[0], so the test passes while hydrating the wrong record and would not catch a find implementation that ignores the requested ID. Make the handler select the requested fruit and assert its ID and corresponding colors (fruit 2 has only color 3), or request fruit 1 if testing its two-color hydration is the goal.

issues.descricao: After saving a host, the component overwrites its category with findById(categoryId); when no category was chosen this is null even though the server saved the uncategorized category, so the row shows no category until reload.

comentarios.texto: The save callback overwrites the category using categoryId even when the server substituted the uncategorized category for a blank selection. Adding a host without choosing a category therefore leaves its category badge empty, and editing it reads an undefined category id despite a valid category_id having been returned. Resolve the category from the saved response's category_id rather than the submitted selection.

When categoryId is null (the default for a new row, or a cleared selection), the controller saves SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id and returns that category_id. This callback instead overwrites host.category with findById(null), making the displayed category disagree with the saved category. Use the category from the save response or its returned category_id rather than the pre-save selection.

Use the saved response's category rather than overwriting it from categoryId after saving. For a new host with no category selected, categoryId is null, while the new controller deliberately saves SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id and returns that ID through the serializer. This callback replaces the hydrated category with findById(null), leaving the row without its actual category until reload (and reopening edit also initializes from that incorrect relationship).

issues.descricao: Hosts saved with a port (allowed by the validation regex) are stored as host:port, but lookup compares only URI.host, so those configured hosts never match and embedding fails for them.

comentarios.texto: Host lookup compares URI.host against a stored value that validation explicitly permits to include a port. Saving example.com:8080 succeeds, but a request from http://example.com:8080 produces URI.host equal to example.com and never matches that record, disabling embedding and retrieval for the configured host. Use a consistent port representation in both storage and lookup.

The validator accepts hosts such as `example.com:8080`, but record_for_host extracts only URI.host (`example.com`) and compares it to the stored port-qualified string. An accepted and saved host therefore never authorizes its corresponding URLs. Normalize the stored and queried authority consistently, including a deliberate port policy.

issues.descricao: EmbeddableHost's host format validation only accepts TLDs of 2-5 letters, so admins cannot add embeddable hosts on longer TLDs like example.technology.
record_for_host queries lower(host) on embeddable_hosts, which has no index on host.
The describe block is named allows_embeddable_host but tests host_allowed?.

sugestoes.texto: The admin/owner gate is built with `&&`, so it only passes when the user is an ADMIN *and* an OWNER simultaneously. `isTeamAdmin` (packages/lib/server/queries/teams/index.ts:270) already returns true for role ADMIN or OWNER, while `isTeamOwner` returns true only for OWNER — so a genuine ADMIN-only team member is wrongly denied the ability to add guests. Replace the `&&` with `||` so either admin or owner role grants access.

`uniqueGuests` (filtered to drop existing attendees and blacklisted emails) is used to create the new attendees, but the unfiltered `guests` array is passed to `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` at line 168. `sendAddGuestsEmails` (packages/emails/email-manager.ts:541) uses `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` to decide between the scheduled-confirmation and add-guests templates, so blacklisted or already-existing emails in the raw array are misclassified as new guests and receives the wrong email/ICS. Pass `uniqueGuests` to `sendAddGuestsEmails` instead.

`isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner` collapses to OWNER-only because `isTeamAdmin` (teams/index.ts:264-284) already matches role ADMIN or OWNER. Non-owner team admins are rejected. This is an access-control bug; use `isTeamAdmin` alone (or `isTeamAdmin || isTeamOwner`) if both roles should pass.

Guests are created from `uniqueGuests` (lines 83-106) but line 168 sends the raw `guests` array to email, so deduplicated guests are not reflected in the notification. Pass `uniqueGuests` to the email call instead.

The blacklist check compares the lowercased `blacklistedGuestEmails` (built at line 71) against the raw, non-normalized `guest` value, so `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` never matches when the submitted email differs in case (`Blocked@x.com` vs `blocked@x.com`). Because `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` accepts `z.string().email()` without lowercasing, an attacker can re-add a deliberately blacklisted guest by changing its casing. Normalize both sides before comparing (e.g. `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest.toLowerCase())`).

issues.descricao: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, so only team owners pass; team admins who are not organizer or attendee are wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN.
issues.textoGolden: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with && instead of ||. WHY: isTeamAdmin returns truthy for role ADMIN or OWNER while isTeamOwner returns true only for OWNER, so the && expression is only true for OWNERs; team ADMINs are treated as unauthorized and get FORBIDDEN when adding guests, contradicting the variable's intent. HOW: use `(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) || (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0))`.

The flag is named `isTeamAdminOrOwner` but is computed with `&&` (both admin AND owner). A team admin who is not the owner, or the owner who is not flagged admin, will fail this check, so the guard at line 54 wrongly throws FORBIDDEN for legitimate admins/owners. Use `||` between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner.

The variable `isTeamAdminOrOwner` names an OR condition, but the code combines `isTeamAdmin(...)` and `isTeamOwner(...)` with `&&`, so it is true only when the user is both admin AND owner. Either the name is wrong or the operator is; as written the permission check at line 54 denies a plain team admin, contradicting what the identifier promises. Use `||` to match the name (or rename if AND is intended).

issues.descricao: The guest blacklist is lowercased but incoming guest emails are compared without normalization, so a blacklisted address submitted with different casing bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and is added and emailed.
issues.textoGolden: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The blacklist is compared case-sensitively against guest input while blacklistedGuestEmails are lowercased. WHY: blacklistedGuestEmails entries are lowercased but the filter compares `guest` verbatim (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`); an authenticated user can add a blacklisted address simply by changing its case (e.g. `Foo@bar.com` vs `foo@bar.com`), bypassing the configured BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restriction. HOW: normalize the guest before comparison, e.g. `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest.toLowerCase())`.

Case-sensitivity bypass of the guest blacklist. `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased on the list side (line 71) but the input side is compared raw: `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` (line 77). A guest email submitted with any different casing (e.g. `Foo@Bar.com` when the blacklist holds `foo@bar.com`) passes the filter and is persisted, defeating BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS. Normalize the input before comparison, e.g. filter on `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest.toLowerCase())` (and likewise lowercase `guest` for the attendee dedup check).

WHAT: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entries are lowercased but the incoming guest string is compared without lowercasing/normalizing. WHY: an attacker bypasses the blocklist with case variation (e.g. Spam@Example.com) and gets added/emailed.

issues.descricao: The server never deduplicates the guests array, so a request with the same email twice inserts duplicate attendee rows for the booking.
issues.textoGolden: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: uniqueGuests filter only dedupes against existing booking.attendees with case-sensitive === and never dedupes duplicates within the input guests array itself (server schema has no uniqueness refine unlike the client). WHY: a request with the same new email twice creates duplicate attendee rows via createMany.

uniqueGuests filters only against existing attendees/blacklist but never dedupes guests[] itself and schema has no uniqueness check. A request like guests=[a@x.com,a@x.com] passes the filter twice and createMany inserts duplicate attendee rows or throws an unhandled DB unique-constraint exception. Dedupe/normalize input (and reject intra-request duplicates) before createMany.

uniqueGuests filters against existing attendees but does not deduplicate addresses within the incoming guests array. A direct mutation with the same new address twice inserts two Attendee records and sends duplicate invitations because the server schema permits duplicates and the Attendee model has no unique booking/email constraint. Deduplicate normalized input before filtering and inserting.

issues.descricao: Check-then-insert without a transaction or unique constraint lets two concurrent addGuests calls for the same email both pass the existing-attendee check and create duplicate attendees.

comentarios.texto: Race condition: findFirst check for existing attendees then booking.update+createMany is not atomic. Two concurrent addGuests calls with the same new email both see it as absent and both insert, creating duplicates. Guard with a unique constraint and handle conflict or run in a transaction/serializable check.

Check-then-insert race: the handler reads `booking.attendees` at the start, filters against it, then inserts in a separate `prisma.booking.update ... createMany` with no transaction or unique guard. Two concurrent addGuests calls for the same guest both see it as absent and both insert, producing duplicate attendees. Wrap the read+filter+insert in a transaction (or rely on a unique constraint on (bookingId, email) and handle the conflict) so concurrent requests cannot both succeed.

issues.descricao: Attendee authorization and existing-attendee dedup compare emails case-sensitively, so an attendee with differently-cased stored email is FORBIDDEN and a case-variant of an existing attendee is added again.

comentarios.texto: Inconsistent email normalization for identity checks. Both the authorization check `attendee.email === user.email` (line 52) and the existing-attendee dedup `guest === attendee.email` (line 76) use strict case-sensitive equality, while emails are treated as case-insensitive everywhere else in this handler (the blacklist block directly below lowercases). Consequence: a legitimate attendee whose stored casing differs from their session email is wrongly FORBIDDEN, and a guest differing from an existing attendee only by case is duplicated rather than filtered. Compare on a normalized form (both sides `.toLowerCase()`), consistent with the blacklist normalization.

issues.descricao: The handler passes the unfiltered guests list to sendAddGuestsEmails, which uses it to pick who gets AttendeeScheduledEmail, so existing attendees included in the request receive a new-booking confirmation instead of the add-guests email.
issues.textoGolden: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) passes the raw input guests instead of the filtered uniqueGuests. WHY: already-existing attendees included in the request are misclassified as newGuests in email-manager and receive AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail (wrong notification).

Dead-transform / wrong input: `uniqueGuests` is computed (dedup vs existing attendees + blacklist) and written to DB, but `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the original `guests`. Existing attendees re-submitted are then `includes()`-matched as new and get AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. Pass `uniqueGuests`.

Pass `uniqueGuests` (the filtered set written to DB) to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of raw `guests`; the email layer assumes newGuests exactly equals newly created attendees for its Scheduled vs AddGuests branch.

issues.descricao: EventManager is created with the requesting user's credentials, so when a non-organizer adds guests the organizer's calendar event is not updated (or the wrong account is used) for references without a credentialId.

comentarios.texto: EventManager is initialized with the requesting user's credentials rather than the booking organizer's credentials. When an attendee or team owner adds guests to a booking whose calendar reference lacks credentialId, updateAllCalendarEvents selects credentials by type from the caller's calendars, so the organizer's event is not updated or the update targets the wrong account. Load credentials for booking.userId and initialize the manager with the booking owner.

issues.descricao: Claims a failing calendar update at addGuests.handler.ts:165 aborts the mutation after guests are persisted; the calendar update path already swallows provider errors.

comentarios.texto: The attendees are written to the database at line 92, but `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` at line 165 runs outside the try/catch. If it throws, the mutation returns an error even though the guests are already persisted, so the DB and the calendar are out of sync. No emails are sent, and a retry then fails with 'emails_must_be_unique_valid'. Catch and handle the calendar update failure after the DB write.

The attendees are already committed to the DB when `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` is awaited without a try/catch. If the calendar sync throws, the mutation returns an error and skips the emails, although the guests were added. The caller sees a failure for a partly applied change and may retry. Handle calendar sync failure as best-effort, as the email send is, or run it before the DB write.

issues.descricao: Claims any attendee can add guests and trigger invites; this is the deliberate permission model of the new feature.

comentarios.texto: Any attendee, matched only by email, is allowed to add arbitrary guests to a booking, and the handler then sends emails and calendar invites on the organizer's behalf. Any attendee can use this to send invites to arbitrary addresses. Restrict the action to the organizer and team admins, or verify that the attendee's email is confirmed.

issues.descricao: The guests array has no server-side size limit, so any authorized caller, including an attendee, can add thousands of guests and trigger an unbounded batch of inserts and emails.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: guests is an unbounded z.array(z.string().email()) with no max length. WHY: any authorized caller (including a mere attendee) can submit thousands of emails causing unbounded createMany inserts plus unbounded Promise.all email fanout in sendAddGuestsEmails.

The mutation accepts an unbounded guest array that is persisted and immediately expanded into concurrent emails to every attendee. For non-seated bookings each email's ICS serializes the full attendee list, so adding N guests creates O(N) concurrent sends and O(N²) aggregate attachment work; repeated additions also resend to all existing attendees. Enforce a server-side guest-count and total-attendee limit before insertion and bound notification concurrency.

issues.descricao: The Remove email tooltip in MultiEmail is a hard-coded English string instead of a translation key.

comentarios.texto: Tooltip content="Remove email" is hard-coded English user-facing text bypassing i18n while surrounding strings in the same file/PR use t(). Wrap it in t() e.g. content={t("remove_email")} and add the key to locales.

`Tooltip content="Remove email"` is a hard-coded English user-facing string, while the surrounding code in this same component routes user text through `t()` (e.g. `t("add_another")` on line 69). This string bypasses the translation mechanism and will never be localised; it should use a translation key.

The new removal tooltip hard-codes `Remove email`, so users in non-English locales see English text even though the neighbouring controls use `t(...)` and this component already obtains `t` from useLocale. Route this tooltip through a translation key (and supply its English translation) rather than using the literal.

issues.descricao: The onError fallback to unable_to_add_guests is unreachable because the template-string message is always truthy.

comentarios.texto: Unreachable fallback: `message` is a template string `${code}: ${...}` which is always truthy, so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` never takes the fallback. Build message conditionally or test the underlying parts for emptiness.

In `onError`, `message` is always a non-empty template string (`"${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}"`), so the fallback `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` is unreachable and the newly added `unable_to_add_guests` translation is never shown. The user is instead shown a raw error code prefix like `BAD_REQUEST: ...` rather than the translated message; the fallback and code prefix handling should be corrected so the intended translated text reaches the user.

The error message is built as a template string, so it is always truthy. The `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback is therefore dead code, and the user can see "undefined: ..." or an untranslated raw message. Use `err.message ? t(err.message) : t("unable_to_add_guests")`.

issues.descricao: After a validation failure followed by a successful add, isInvalidEmail stays true, so the stale emails_must_be_unique_valid error shows the next time the dialog is opened.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: addGuestsMutation onSuccess resets multiEmailValue and closes the dialog but never resets isInvalidEmail. WHY: after one failed validation the red emails_must_be_unique_valid error persists on the next open/successful add.

issues.descricao: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings, so hosts and attendees receive add-guests emails even when standard emails are disabled.
issues.textoGolden: The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

issues.descricao: The add-guests handler omits booking.iCalUID from the CalendarEvent, so the add-guests emails' .ics attachments use booking.uid as UID and recipients' calendars treat them as a new event rather than an update of the original booking invite.
The addGuests FORBIDDEN error uses the translation key you_do_not_have_permission, which is missing from the locale files, so the dialog shows the raw key to users.
The comment in MultiEmailLazy.tsx ("These are like 40kb") is copied from the phone input lazy loader and does not apply to MultiEmail, which only uses existing UI components.
addGuests does not check the booking status, so guests can be added to cancelled or rejected bookings, which updates calendars and emails invitations for events that no longer exist.
Guest email uniqueness is checked case-sensitively, so case variants of the same address are accepted as distinct guests (and slip past the lowercased blacklist).
Adding guests ignores `seatsPerTimeSlot`, so a seated event can exceed its configured capacity; reject when attendees plus new guests exceed the seat limit.

sugestoes.texto: tagDeviceUI caches the device cache key via localCache.SetDefault (impl.go:87) before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice, so when an over-limit device gets ErrDeviceLimitReached the key is still cached and the new `return err` is only surfaced once. Every later request from that same device within the 29-minute TTL hits the cache, returns nil, and Authenticate succeeds — so the configurable device limit only blocks each new device once instead of continuously. Move the SetDefault after a successful CreateOrUpdateDevice (or delete the key on error) so an untagged device is never treated as tagged.

CreateOrUpdateDevice reads the device count and then inserts in a separate statement with no lock, transaction, or unique constraint, so the limit is a check-then-act race. Two concurrent requests from different new devices can both observe count < deviceLimit and both insert, letting the number of tracked devices exceed the configured limit. Enforce the cap atomically (e.g. lock the row range / use a serialized counter, or accept and document the best-effort semantics).
Cache is populated before the DB write in tagDeviceUI, so a device rejected by the limit is still treated as tagged on the next request, enabling a device-limit bypass.
CreateOrUpdateDevice performs a non-transactional count-then-write, creating a race condition in the device-limit enforcement.
CreateOrUpdateDevice performs a non-transactional count-then-write, creating a race condition in the device-limit enforcement.

issues.descricao: The device limit check counts devices and then inserts in separate non-atomic steps, so concurrent requests from new devices can all pass the check and exceed the configured limit.
issues.textoGolden: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.

comentarios.texto: The limit check counts devices and then inserts in separate steps with no lock or transaction. Concurrent requests from new devices can all see count < limit and all insert, so the limit is exceeded. Make the count-and-insert atomic, for example with a conditional INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*)) < limit.

The device limit check is a non-atomic count followed by an insert. Concurrent requests from different new devices can all see count < limit and all insert, so the number of devices exceeds deviceLimit. Make the check and insert atomic, for example with a conditional INSERT ... SELECT WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*)) < limit, or serialize the check and insert under a lock.

WHAT: CreateOrUpdateDevice does check-then-act (CountDevices then INSERT/UPSERT) with no lock, transaction, or unique-guard when deviceLimit>0. WHY: Two concurrent new-device requests can both observe count < limit and both insert, exceeding the configured limit and breaking the enforcement contract. HOW: Enforce atomically (e.g., conditional insert guarded by count in one statement/transaction with serializable lock, or re-check count on conflict).

issues.descricao: Device slots are keyed by the client-controlled X-Grafana-Device-Id header with no validation or rate limiting, so an anonymous caller can fill the limit with fake IDs and deny anonymous access to every new legitimate device.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Device slots counted toward deviceLimit are keyed by the unauthenticated X-Grafana-Device-Id header (read in impl.go TagDevice) with no validation or rate-limit. WHY: Any anonymous caller can mint arbitrary device IDs to fill the table up to the limit, after which all legitimate new anonymous devices get ErrDeviceLimitReached and authentication is denied — a trivial anonymous-access DoS introduced by the limit. HOW: Do not let a single client consume many slots (e.g., bind slot consumption to IP/fingerprint, rate-limit new-device creation, or require proof of distinct device).

issues.descricao: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only checks that a new device is rejected at the limit and never verifies that an existing device can still be updated at the limit.

comentarios.texto: The at-limit call reuses a brand-new device ID ("keep") that was never inserted, so it only reaches updateDevice's `rowsAffected == 0` -> ErrDeviceLimitReached branch. The success branch of the newly added updateDevice (an existing device still being updated while the store is at the limit) is never exercised by any test — every other call uses deviceLimit 0, so updateDevice is never invoked. A regression that made updateDevice always affect 0 rows, use a wrong WHERE/SET, or unconditionally return ErrDeviceLimitReached whenever limit>0 would leave this and all other tests green. Add a case that, after the store is at the limit, calls CreateOrUpdateDevice again with the SAME DeviceID and asserts require.NoError (and ideally that client_ip/user_agent/updated_at were changed), so the update path is actually verified.

TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only checks that a new device is rejected at the limit. It would still pass if updateDevice always returned ErrDeviceLimitReached, because it never re-submits the existing device (DeviceID "32mdo31deeqwes") at the limit. Add a call that updates the existing device with a new UserAgent or UpdatedAt, require NoError, and check the stored row changed.

issues.descricao: tagDeviceUI caches the device key before CreateOrUpdateDevice; when the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the entry stays, so the next request from the same device skips the limit check and authenticates for up to 29 minutes.
issues.textoGolden: The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. If `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry remains set, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit until the cache expires after 29 minutes.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: TagDevice failures that triggered the new ErrDeviceLimitReached early-return are not permanent, because tagDeviceUI (impl.go:87) writes the device key into localCache BEFORE CreateOrUpdateDevice (impl.go:93) and never evicts it on error; tagDeviceUI returns early on any cache hit (impl.go:83-84). WHY: the first request from a new over-limit device is denied, but the poisoned cache makes every subsequent request from that same device skip the limit check entirely and authenticate successfully, so the configurable device limit is bypassed by simply retrying. HOW: only set the cache key after CreateOrUpdateDevice returns nil (e.g. move a.localCache.SetDefault after the successful DB write, or delete the key when it returns ErrDeviceLimitReached).

TagDevice now propagates ErrDeviceLimitReached to deny an over-limit anonymous device, but tagDeviceUI (impl.go:83-95) records the device in localCache at line 87 *before* calling a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice. When the store rejects the device with ErrDeviceLimitReached, the key is already cached, so the next request for that same device returns early at line 83 with a nil error and the device is admitted. The limit therefore only blocks the first request and is silently bypassed on retry. Fix by only setting the cache entry after CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds (move SetDefault after the store call), or by removing/not caching the key on failure.

The new authentication gate accepts retries from devices that were rejected by the limit because tagDeviceUI inserts the cache entry before CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds. At capacity, the first request with a new X-Grafana-Device-Id fails, but subsequent requests with that same ID hit the 29-minute cache and receive an anonymous identity without admission to the device store. Cache only successful admissions, and ensure concurrent requests cannot treat an in-progress admission as successful.

issues.descricao: Device tagging now runs synchronously in Authenticate, adding DB round-trips on cache-miss anonymous requests where it used to be fire-and-forget.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Anonymous.Authenticate changed from fire-and-forget goroutine TagDevice to synchronous TagDevice(ctx) that runs CountDevices + INSERT/UPDATE inline. WHY: Every cache-miss anonymous authentication now blocks on two DB round-trips in the login hot path, adding latency and DB load per request where previously auth returned immediately. HOW: Restore async tagging for the non-limit path or at least decouple denial from the hot path (e.g., async count with cached count, or only synchronously enforce when near limit).

issues.descricao: The new auth.anonymous device_limit setting has no entry in conf/defaults.ini, so the GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT environment override is ignored and the limit stays 0.

comentarios.texto: The new device_limit setting is read without adding a corresponding key to conf/defaults.ini. applyEnvVariableOverrides only visits keys already present in the loaded INI and runs before readAuthSettings, so setting GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT alone is ignored and leaves the limit at zero, disabling enforcement. Add an uncommented device_limit = 0 entry under auth.anonymous in defaults.ini so the standard environment override mechanism can apply it.

issues.descricao: The anonymous device limit is enforced only through TagDevice, which returns nil when the client-controlled device ID header is missing, so requests without the header authenticate anonymously regardless of the configured limit.

The doc comment on updateDevice says it updates a device "updated between the given times", but the function takes no times, computes the 30-day window itself and returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when no row matches.
updateDevice prepends the query to the captured args inside the retried DB callback, so a SQLite lock retry runs Exec with the query duplicated in the arguments and the update fails.

sugestoes.texto: The header `if` block is closed with `<%- end if %>`, which ERB compiles to the literal Ruby `end if`; `end` cannot take an `if` modifier and a bare `if` with no condition is a syntax error. The template therefore fails to compile whenever the `best` view is rendered (topic_id found), returning a 500 instead of the embedded comments, and the controller specs miss it because they do not render views. Change it to `<%- end %>`.

Posts imported via `TopicEmbed.import`/`import_remote` are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and this branch returns `raw` directly, skipping Discourse's rendering/sanitization pipeline. The raw external HTML is then emitted unescaped (`<%= raw post.cooked %>` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19 and via the cooked serializer on the main topic page), so any `<script>`/event-handler markup present in the fetched article or RSS item executes on the Discourse origin for every reader. Sanitize the imported HTML (e.g., run it through the cook pipeline or an allowlist sanitizer) before storing it as `cooked` instead of storing raw HTML verbatim.

`i.content` is nil for RSS 2.0 feeds (SimpleRSS exposes the item body as `description`, reserving `content` for Atom entries), so `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError and aborts the whole poll. Since the feature is documented as supporting 'RSS/ATOM', fall back to the description when content is absent.

`raw post.cooked` renders imported feed HTML verbatim: for posts imported via `TopicEmbed.import` the cook_method is `raw_html`, so `Post#cook` returns the un-sanitized feed body (poll_feed.rb:35 stores `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` directly). A malicious or compromised third-party feed can therefore inject `<script>` that executes on the Discourse origin inside the embed iframe, enabling stored XSS; sanitize the imported HTML before storing or escape it here.

issues.descricao: The postMessage handler in embed.js checks the sender with discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin), a substring test instead of exact origin equality, so a page on an origin that is a substring of the Discourse URL can send forged discourse-resize messages to the embedding page.
issues.textoGolden: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.

comentarios.texto: The message-origin check uses substring matching: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`. Any origin that is a substring of discourseUrl is accepted (e.g. discourseUrl `https://discourse.example.com` accepts origin `https://discourse`), so a malicious page can post `discourse-resize` messages into the embed. Compare against the iframe's actual origin exactly (`e.origin !== expectedOrigin`) instead of a substring test.
Uses indexOf containment instead of origin equality, but it cannot be bypassed.

WHAT: postMessage origin check is reversed (`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)===-1`) instead of strict origin equality. WHY: any e.origin that is a substring of discourseUrl passes, letting a foreign iframe drive `iframe.height` handling and future message branches.

issues.descricao: The referer and embed_url host checks compare against SiteSetting.embeddable_host case-sensitively, so a host differing only in case is rejected even though hostnames are case-insensitive.

comentarios.texto: Host identity is compared case-sensitively: `URI(request.referer).host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. Hostnames are case-insensitive, so a referer such as `http://EVILTROUT.COM/...` never matches the configured `eviltrout.com` (and the same flaw exists in lib/topic_retriever.rb:15 for `URI(@embed_url).host`). Normalize both sides with downcase before comparing so case variations of the same host are treated identically.

The referer/host comparison does not lowercase either side, so a mixed-case host is wrongly rejected. The reviewer notes this fails closed and is not a bypass. Normalize case on both sides of the host comparison (e.g. downcase both) to avoid false rejections. The same issue applies to topic_retriever.rb.

The host comparison does not lowercase either side, so a mixed-case host is wrongly rejected. This fails closed and is not a bypass. Normalize case on both sides of the comparison (e.g. downcase both) to avoid false rejections.

issues.descricao: PollFeed reads i.content.scrub for every feed item, so items without a content element (common in RSS feeds that only have description) raise NoMethodError and abort the import of the remaining items.
issues.textoGolden: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every feed item has a `content` element. WHY: many RSS 2.0 items expose only `<description>` (simple-rss returns nil for `content`), so `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError and, because the job is `sidekiq_options retry: false`, the entire hourly feed import for all items is aborted. HOW: fall back to the available field, e.g. `(i.content || i.description || i.summary).to_s.scrub`, and skip items whose body is blank.

The feed item is consumed unconditionally: url = i.link, then i.title, and content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub). SimpleRSS item accessors raise NoMethodError when the element is absent (RSS 2.0 feeds frequently carry only <description>, no <content>, and some items have no <link>/<title>), so a single malformed or content-less item aborts the whole hourly job with an unhandled exception instead of skipping it. The code already anticipates a blank link (line 33 fallback) but reads i.content/i.title without a nil guard; use i.content.to_s (or fall back to i.description/summary) and skip items whose content is blank.

`i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError when a feed item has no content (only a description). The exception aborts the whole poll, so every item after it is never imported. Fall back to `i.content || i.description`, skip items with blank content, and rescue per item.

issues.descricao: Posts imported from RSS or remote pages use cook_method raw_html, which makes Post#cook return the raw HTML without sanitization, and the embed view outputs it with raw post.cooked, allowing stored XSS from imported content.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: the new `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` makes `Post#cook` return completely unsanitized HTML, and Jobs::PollFeed stores untrusted feed content this way (poll_feed.rb:35-36 → TopicEmbed.import, unlike import_remote which sanitizes via Readability's tag/attribute whitelist). WHY: the stored `cooked` value is then emitted with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19, and that page is served from the forum's own origin — so a malicious/compromised RSS feed item containing `<script>` or `onerror=` runs attacker JavaScript in the forum origin and can read cookies/session and perform authenticated actions (stored XSS). HOW: sanitize the raw HTML before persisting it (e.g. run the feed content through the same HTML sanitizer used for regular posts, or restrict the raw_html cook path to trusted, pre-sanitized sources only).

WHAT: Post#cook returns raw verbatim for cook_method raw_html, skipping the cooking/sanitization pipeline and plugin filters. WHY: any RSS/readability HTML imported via TopicEmbed is rendered unsanitized in embed/best.html.erb, executing attacker script in the Discourse origin.

Feed-provided HTML is persisted with raw_html cooking after only Nokogiri parsing and URL rewriting, which do not sanitize scripts or event-handler attributes. A malicious feed entry containing executable HTML is stored as post.cooked and executed under the forum origin when rendered, including through the new raw cooked embed view. Sanitize imported HTML with an explicit safe tag, attribute and URL-scheme allowlist before storing it or returning it from the raw_html cooking path.

issues.descricao: TopicEmbed.import appends a footer that interpolates the URL unescaped into an <a href='...'> tag in raw HTML that is later rendered unsanitized, so a crafted URL can inject markup; it also appends to contents with << without handling nil.
issues.textoGolden: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: TopicEmbed.import interpolates feed-controlled url unescaped into raw HTML (`#{url}`) and stores feed HTML as raw_html. WHY: url passing /^https?\:\/\// can still contain `'`, `>` or script, and RSS content is never sanitized, giving stored XSS when rendered via `raw post.cooked`. HOW: HTML-escape url and sanitize content instead of raw_html passthrough.

TopicEmbed.import interpolates feed-controlled url unescaped into HTML link stored with cook_method raw_html (Post#cook returns raw, bypassing pipeline) and rendered with raw post.cooked: XSS via quote/script break-out. Escape url for text and attribute contexts before storing.

The url is interpolated unescaped into `#{url}`. The post is stored with cook_method raw_html and rendered with `raw post.cooked`, so a url containing a quote or markup is output as live HTML. Escape it with ERB::Util.html_escape (or CGI.escapeHTML) for both the href and the link text.

issues.descricao: TopicEmbed.import appends the footer with contents <<, mutating the caller's string in place instead of building a new string.

comentarios.texto: `contents <<` mutates the caller's string in place. This raises FrozenError for frozen strings and appends the footer twice if the same string is imported again. Use `contents = contents + ...` instead.

issues.descricao: TopicEmbed.import checks for an existing embed and then creates the post and TopicEmbed without handling the unique-index conflict, so two concurrent imports of the same URL make one job fail with RecordNotUnique.

comentarios.texto: TopicEmbed.import does a check-then-insert on embed_url (where(...).first, then TopicEmbed.create!) with no rescue for the unique index declared on topic_embeds.embed_url. The only guard against concurrent intake is the Redis throttle in TopicRetriever, which is bypassed for staff (retrieve_topic.rb:17 passes no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)) and can expire while a slow retrieval (which may synchronously run a full PollFeed, topic_retriever.rb:41) is still running. Two interleaved retrievals for the same URL both see embed.blank? and both attempt creation; the loser raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, which is unhandled anywhere in the job path, breaking execution. Guard the create against the race (rescue/retry on RecordNotUnique, or use find_or_create_by on embed_url inside the transaction) so concurrent retrievals cannot raise.

Make creation idempotent under concurrent imports. Two workers can both read no embed at line 15 and create posts before attempting the same unique embed_url insert. The unique index correctly rolls back the losing transaction, but its unhandled uniqueness exception aborts that job (and potentially the rest of a feed polling run). This is reachable when scheduled polling overlaps retrieval-triggered polling; the per-URL retrieval throttle does not serialize those paths. Handle the conflict outside the transaction and return the winning embed/post, or serialize imports for the URL.

Race on check-then-create: two concurrent imports both see TopicEmbed.where(embed_url:url).first blank, both create Post + TopicEmbed.create!. Unique index on embed_url then raises RecordNotUnique (unhandled) or creates duplicates. Need atomic find-or-create / rescue unique violation.

issues.descricao: When the embedded post has been deleted, TopicEmbed.import's update path passes a nil embed.post to PostRevisor and crashes on every later import of that URL.

comentarios.texto: On the update path `embed.post` can be nil if the post was deleted. `PostRevisor.new(nil)` then raises NoMethodError, and every later import of that URL fails the same way. Guard against a nil post, for example by skipping the revision or recreating the topic.

WHAT: update path uses `embed.post` without nil guard then `PostRevisor.new(post)`. WHY: if the first post was deleted, post is nil and revise! dereferences nil, crashing feed-poll updates instead of recreating/skipping.

Orphan-post crash on update path: post = embed.post can be nil if the post/topic was deleted, then PostRevisor.new(nil).revise! raises NoMethodError. Must handle missing post (recreate or skip) instead of assuming present.

issues.descricao: Claims import_remote crashes on unparseable pages (nil content) and dead URLs because it does no nil check or network error handling around open(url).read.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: import_remote passes `doc.content` (and title) directly to import where `contents <<` assumes a String, with no nil check or network-error handling around `open(url).read`. WHY: unparseable pages (nil content) raise NoMethodError and dead URLs raise OpenURI errors, crashing RetrieveTopic/Disqus imports with no topic created.

issues.descricao: absolutize_urls only handles root-relative paths: protocol-relative URLs like //cdn.example.com/x.png are rewritten to http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png and path-relative links are left unresolved, breaking links and images in imported posts.

comentarios.texto: The URL rewrite treats protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/image.jpg` as paths on the article host, producing `http://article-host/cdn.example.com/image.jpg`. Imported images and links using protocol-relative external URLs therefore point to the wrong server. Resolve both href and src using URI joining against the article URL, which also handles ordinary relative paths correctly.

Resolve relative href/src references with URI joining rather than handling only leading slashes. For an article at http://example.com/blog/article, href='next' and src='images/photo.jpg' remain relative and resolve against the forum instead of the imported article. Moreover, '//cdn.example.com/photo.jpg' is rewritten to 'http://example.com/cdn.example.com/photo.jpg'. Both yield incorrect links/images in imported posts; apply proper URI resolution to both anchors and images.

absolutize_urls treats any href or src starting with '/' as site-relative and strips all leading slashes. Protocol-relative URLs like '//cdn.example.com/a.png' are rewritten to 'http://site/cdn.example.com/a.png', which is broken. Skip values starting with '//' (or prefix them with the scheme) and only rewrite single-slash paths.

issues.descricao: The embed view formats post dates with a hard-coded strftime pattern, so users in non-English locales see English month names and a fixed order while the rest of the view is translated.

comentarios.texto: The post date uses a hard-coded strftime format `"%e %b %Y"`. `%b` emits English month abbreviations (Jan, Feb, ...) no matter what locale the viewer is in, so the date is frozen to en-US while the surrounding strings in this same view are localized via I18n.t. This is a locale-pinned user-facing format; it should be localized (e.g. via the app's localized date helper / l( ) rather than a literal strftime pattern).

Use a localized date formatter rather than strftime("%e %b %Y"). %b produces English month abbreviations and the fixed day-month-year order ignores the selected locale, although the neighbouring header and footer labels are translated. Embedded comments therefore show English-formatted dates for users of other locales.
Date uses strftime("%e %b %Y") hard-coding one locale's month names/order while neighbouring strings go through I18n.t. Use I18n.l with a locale date format so non-English users see localized dates.

issues.descricao: The Disqus importer now creates topics through TopicEmbed.import_remote, dropping the thread's created_at and the category option and requiring a live HTTP fetch per thread, so imported topics get wrong dates/categories and a dead link aborts the import.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Disqus import replaced PostCreator (title/raw/created_at/category) with `TopicEmbed.import_remote` per thread, dropping category_id, created_at, and strip handling. WHY: imported topics lose categories/timestamps and now require a live HTTP fetch per thread, failing when links are dead.

Preserve the Disqus thread creation timestamp when switching to TopicEmbed.import_remote. The previous PostCreator call passed `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])`, but this replacement passes only the title, and TopicEmbed.import_remote/import never forward a timestamp to PostCreator. Imported historical topics now get the migration time as their initial post creation date while their replies retain historical dates, losing the importer's chronological fidelity. Extend the import options to forward created_at and pass the thread timestamp here.

The Disqus import now calls TopicEmbed.import_remote instead of PostCreator. This silently drops the `--category` option and the `created_at` from the Disqus thread, and the `--category` method_option was removed from the CLI. It also now makes a live HTTP fetch of every thread link, and `open(url)` raises on a failure that previously could not happen, aborting the whole import. Keep the category and date handling, and rescue fetch errors per thread.

issues.descricao: Every retrieval of an article not yet embedded synchronously polls and imports the entire RSS feed, and since throttling is per URL, many different article requests repeat the full feed download and processing.

comentarios.texto: Every uncached article retrieval synchronously downloads and processes the complete configured feed before fetching the article. Because the retrieval throttle is keyed by individual embed URL, simultaneous requests for different articles each repeat the feed download and all per-item database lookups/imports, multiplying worker load by the number of requests times feed size. Coalesce feed polling with a feed-wide throttle or lock and reuse its recent results instead of executing a full poll per article.

issues.descricao: The 'is 404 without an embed_url' spec never sets an embeddable host, so the request is rejected by ensure_embeddable before the embed_url check runs, and the test would pass even without that check.

comentarios.texto: The test is named 'is 404 without an embed_url' but passes for the wrong reason: it never sets embeddable_host, which defaults to '' so the before_filter `ensure_embeddable` raises at the blank-host check before `params.require(:embed_url)` is reached. The request is rejected regardless of whether the embed_url requirement exists, so the test would still pass if that requirement were removed. Stub a valid embeddable_host here so the failure is actually attributable to the missing embed_url.

The missing-embed_url test does not establish a valid embeddable host and referer, so ensure_embeddable rejects this request before best reaches params.require(:embed_url). It also only checks non-success despite claiming a 404. Removing the required-parameter check would therefore leave this test green. Configure an allowed host/referer for this case and assert the intended missing-parameter response.

The 'is 404 without an embed_url' test never sets embeddable_host, so ensure_embeddable rejects the request before params.require(:embed_url) runs. It passes without the embed_url check. Stub embeddable_host and the referer so the missing param is the only failure cause.

issues.descricao: The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' specs leave feed_polling_enabled at its false default, so they never reach the condition they name and would pass with those checks deleted.

comentarios.texto: The three 'requires ...' tests do not isolate the guard they name: each stubs only one setting to falsy while the other two remain falsy by default, so poll_feed is never called even if the named check were deleted. Stub the other two settings to truthy values in each test so removing the named guard would cause poll_feed to run and fail the test.

These two tests do not verify the conditions they name. `execute` is guarded by `feed_polling_enabled? && feed_polling_url.present? && embed_by_username.present?`, and feed_polling_enabled defaults to false. Neither test stubs feed_polling_enabled? to true, so the guard short-circuits at the first clause and poll_feed is never called no matter what feed_polling_url/embed_by_username are. Both would still pass if the URL/username checks were deleted entirely. Stub `SiteSetting.stubs(:feed_polling_enabled?).returns(true)` in each so the specific condition under test is actually reached.

The URL and username prerequisite tests never enable feed polling (whose configured default is false) or supply the other required setting. execute consequently short-circuits at feed_polling_enabled? and never evaluates the prerequisite each test claims to cover. Both tests still pass if their corresponding presence checks are removed. Set all other prerequisites to valid values before making only the setting under test absent, so the poll_feed.never expectation actually detects removal of that guard.

issues.descricao: PollFeed.feed_key computes a per-feed cache key that is never used, so the feed is re-fetched and re-processed every hour without a modified-since check.
The embed layout references the 'embed' stylesheet and embed.js, but neither is in config.assets.precompile, so with precompiled assets in production the embed page fails to load them.
The retrieve throttle is keyed by the full embed URL, so an anonymous client can vary the query string on the embeddable host to bypass it and make the server create an unbounded number of topics.

The "requires feed_polling_enabled?" spec leaves feed_polling_url and embed_by_username at their blank defaults, so poll_feed is skipped regardless and the test would pass even without the enabled check.
TopicEmbed.import_remote fetches the embed URL with open(url).read and no timeout or size limit, so a slow or huge remote page can block the background job and exhaust memory.
The retrieve throttle sets the Redis key with setnx and sets its TTL in a separate expire call, so a crash between the two leaves a key without expiry that blocks retrieval of that URL forever.
`import_remote` fetches the embed URL with open-uri, which follows redirects, so the embeddable-host check on the initial URL can be bypassed to reach internal services (SSRF).

sugestoes.texto: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` raises KeyError when the existing active Integration has no `sender` key in its metadata. The codebase confirms this case occurs — test_basic_flow asserts pipeline-created metadata has no `sender`, and installation.py:44 explicitly guards `if "sender" not in integration.metadata` — so the branch that reaches this line (active Integration with matching external_id but no linked OrganizationIntegration) would crash the dispatch with a 500 instead of showing the intended failure dialog. Use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and reject (return the error view) when it is missing.

The OAuth `state` is set to `pipeline.signature`, which `Pipeline.__init__` computes as `md5_text(*pipe_ids)` over the view class names (pipeline/base.py:132-133) — a constant identical for every user and request, and the callback only re-checks it against that same constant. This makes the state predictable and removes the per-request anti-CSRF binding that OAuth state is meant to provide; the canonical flow in identity/oauth2.py generates `secrets.token_hex()` and validates against the value stored in pipeline state (`fetch_state("state")`). Generate a random state, bind it into the pipeline, and compare the callback's `state` against that stored value.

`get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` performs an unguarded HTTP call whose implementation (`sentry/identity/github/provider.py`) calls `resp.raise_for_status()` and `.json()`. A non-2xx response (invalid/expired token, rate limit, API error) or a non-JSON body raises uncaught, so the installation flow returns a 500 instead of the intended error page the surrounding code carefully produces for other failures. Wrap this call in try/except (or add error handling in `get_user_info`) and route failures to the `error(...)` view.

The newly added GitHub-user validation only runs when an `Integration` record already exists; when `Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id)` raises `DoesNotExist`, `dispatch` returns `pipeline.next_step()` and finishes the pipeline without ever comparing the OAuth-authenticated user to who installed the app. An attacker who supplies an installation_id before the 'installation created' webhook materializes the Integration (delayed/failed webhook, intentional race) binds that installation to the session's organization, bypassing the very mismatch check this PR adds. Validate the authenticated user against the GitHub installation/account obtained from the API in this branch as well (or defer binding until the sender is known).

issues.descricao: error() calls _(error_short) on a variable and callers pass plain literals, so the short error strings are no longer extractable for translation.

comentarios.texto: The helper calls `_(error_short)` on a variable, and callers pass plain string literals. The translation extractor cannot see these strings, so the short error messages sent to the user are no longer translatable; the old code wrapped the literals directly in `_()`. Mark the literals with gettext_lazy at the call sites and the default, and pass them through without wrapping again.

error_short strings bypass translation extraction: _(error_short) uses a variable so makemessages cannot collect them. Wrap literals at definition/call sites, e.g. error_short=_("Invalid installation request.") and pass _("...") literals, then use data error value directly without re-wrapping.

Translate the short-message literals at their definition/call sites instead of calling `_(error_short)` on a variable. Django's message extraction cannot extract the default `"Invalid installation request."` or the plain-string arguments at the two call sites from this dynamic gettext invocation. The existing pending-deletion and already-installed messages previously appeared directly inside `_()`; this refactor removes their extraction sites, and the new default message cannot enter translation catalogs. Use a translated default and translated arguments, then place `error_short` directly into the payload so these user-facing errors remain localizable.

issues.descricao: The org parameter of error()/get_document_origin is actually the active-organization context, not an Organization, so the name is misleading.

comentarios.texto: The parameter is named `org` but the code treats it as the pipeline's active-organization context: it dereferences `org.organization` and every caller (error() and the GitHubInstallation sites) passes `self.active_organization`, not an Organization. The name misstates the argument's type/contract — a caller following the name and passing a real Organization would hit AttributeError on `.organization`. Rename the parameter (e.g. `active_organization`) and correct the corresponding name in `error()` at line 131 so the two signatures match what is actually passed.

issues.descricao: The GitHub OAuth state is pipeline.signature, a static md5 of the pipeline view names, instead of a per-attempt random nonce, so it gives no CSRF protection.
issues.textoGolden: OAuth state uses pipeline.signature (static) instead of a per-request random value

comentarios.texto: The OAuth state is pipeline.signature, which Pipeline.__init__ computes solely from pipeline view class names and therefore shares across all users and installation attempts. An attacker can obtain an OAuth code for their own GitHub account and send a callback using this known state to a victim with an active installation pipeline, binding the attacker's GitHub identity to the victim's flow instead of rejecting the forged callback. Generate a random per-attempt nonce, store it in pipeline state, and validate that nonce on the OAuth callback.

Do not use pipeline.signature as OAuth state. It is a deterministic MD5 of the pipeline identifiers, not an unpredictable nonce tied to this user's authorization attempt (the tests reuse it across users). An attacker can know the expected state and submit a callback containing a code authorized under the attacker's GitHub account, defeating the OAuth login-CSRF protection and the intended binding to the installing user. Generate a cryptographically random per-attempt state, store it in the session/pipeline, and validate and consume it on callback.

issues.descricao: The new OAuth step's token exchange and user lookup are not wrapped in error handling, so GitHub/network failures surface as 500s instead of the installation-failed page.

comentarios.texto: The token request is executed outside the try block. If GitHub's token endpoint is unavailable or the request fails with a connection/timeout error, safe_urlopen raises before the guarded response parsing is reached, and this new installation step returns an unhandled server error instead of the installation-failed response. Include the request itself in the error handling and handle the relevant transport exceptions.

WHAT: safe_urlopen token exchange and get_user_info() (which calls resp.raise_for_status()) are called with no exception handling. WHY: Any network error, timeout, or non-2xx from GitHub bubbles up as an unhandled exception and 500s the install instead of rendering the invalid-request page. HOW: Wrap the exchange plus get_user_info in try/except and return error() on failure.

safe_urlopen() and get_user_info() are called outside any try/except, so network errors, non-2xx responses, or API failures raise unhandled exceptions instead of returning error(). Wrap the token exchange + user-info fetch in try/except and return error() on failure, matching the handled missing-access_token path.

issues.descricao: When no Integration exists yet for the installation_id the pipeline advances without comparing the OAuth user to the installer, bypassing the new ownership check.

comentarios.texto: The missing Integration branch advances the pipeline without verifying that github_authenticated_user installed the supplied installation_id. When the installation webhook has not created a record, or the local record was deleted, finish_pipeline calls build_integration using app credentials and attaches the installation without checking the OAuth user's access, allowing a user with another account's installation ID to bypass the new ownership check. Fail closed until trusted installer information is available and apply the ownership check before every successful next_step.

The record-absent path advances the pipeline before checking whether the authenticated GitHub user installed this app. Installation IDs arrive from the request, and a missing Integration record (for example before the installation webhook is processed) does not establish ownership. As a result, this path can attach an installation belonging to a different GitHub user despite the new authenticity check. Verify the authenticated user's authorization for the installation before advancing in this branch too, rather than relying on the webhook-created record existing.

When no Integration row exists for the installation_id, the code calls next_step() without comparing the OAuth-authenticated GitHub user to the installer. An attacker can supply an installation_id they do not own before the installation webhook has created the row, and bypass the new verification. Do not skip the check in this branch. Either fail closed, or verify ownership another way, for example by confirming the user can access the installation through the GitHub API.

issues.descricao: The installer check indexes integration.metadata['sender']['login'] without checking that sender exists, raising KeyError for integrations created without sender metadata.
issues.textoGolden: The code attempts to access integration.metadata[sender][login] without checking for the existence of the sender key. This causes a KeyError for integrations where the sender metadata was not set during creation

comentarios.texto: integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] is indexed without checking that "sender" exists, so an ACTIVE integration whose metadata has no sender raises KeyError (500) here. metadata["sender"] is only populated when state.get("sender") is set (integration.py:376-377), and the only writer of that state is the installation webhook (webhook.py:202-208); integrations created through the pipeline itself carry no sender (confirmed by installation.py:44 which explicitly guards `if "sender" not in integration.metadata`, and by the pipeline-created integration in test_integration.py:730-743). Previously this branch only bound state and called pipeline.next_step(), so this crash is newly introduced. Fix: guard the lookup, e.g. `if pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") != (integration.metadata.get("sender") or {}).get("login"):` and decide the desired fallback when sender is absent.

`integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` can raise KeyError. build_integration (line 376-377) only sets metadata["sender"] when state.get("sender") is truthy, so an existing Integration without a sender entry makes this subscripting throw an unhandled KeyError (500) instead of routing to the intended error page. Use `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` (and treat a missing sender as a failed verification) so the mismatch/absence case returns error() rather than crashing.
